text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Junior social affairs minister calls for concrete measures to stop increase of pension fund premiums. (p1)
- Bank insurer ING Group withdraws from takeover talks with U.S. investment bank Dillon Read. (p1)
- Amsterdam Exchanges AEX reaches new all-time high at 796.84 boosted by lower U.S. PPI. (p1)
- Dutch pension fund umbrella groups not concerned that inflation fears will undermine pension system. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell rejects claims by environmental lobby group Milieudefensie that it has not kept promises made regarding its Nigerian activities. (p1)
- Retail and services group Vendex books 35 pct Q1 turnover growth boosted by two takeovers. (p3)
- British Telecom threatens to take KPN to court if the Dutch Telecom group's interconnection tariffs remain too high. (p3)
- Insurer Delta Lloyd's first quarter net pressured by large fires. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Britain's association COTS halts mediation between couples unable to have baby and surrogate mother after conflict with Dutch couple. (p1)
- ABN Amro subsidiary Hoare Govett to take a 49 pct stake in Thailand's investment bank Asia Securities Trading. (p2)
- Philips Electronics and steel concern Hoogovens sell their joint subsidiary Amefo to U.S. Quanex group. (p2)
- Investors react negatively to expensive takeover of Aurum by automation company Baan. (p33) DE TELEGRAAF
- PM Wim Kok takes over from health minister on out home health care system reform. (p3)
- Inland revenue to start offensive against fraud with temp agencies' expense claims. (p6)
- Services group Vedior aims at large investors for its new share issue. (p33)
- Clothes producer Vilenzo is forecasting a ten million guilder profit this year. (p37) TROUW
- Conflict mounts between traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma and Labour party over introducing competition in public transport. (p4) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chemical industry is to give grants to students in an attempt to get them interested in chemistry studies. (p1)
- The Netherlands is the most attractive country for investment and business according to Economic Intelligence Unit EIU. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
